findings.claim: When GPT-4 generates text, it assigns probabilities to every possible next word.
findings.issue: GPT-4 is used only as a generic illustration of an autoregressive model producing a probability distribution, which is fine. However, as of 2026-07-05 GPT-4 is a superseded model (later releases such as GPT-4o and successors exist). The sentence does not present GPT-4 as the current frontier lineup, so it is not blocking, but swapping in a current-generation example (or making it model-agnostic) would keep the page from looking dated.

findings.claim: A distilled model might achieve 90% of the teacher's quality at 10% of the computational cost.
findings.issue: Presented as an illustrative 'might achieve' hypothetical rather than a measured benchmark, so acceptable. For context, the cited DistilBERT paper reports the concrete figures of ~40% size reduction while retaining ~97% of language-understanding capability and being ~60% faster; the round '90%/10%' numbers are indicative, not sourced to a specific result.

reasons: fact-check FAILED twice — original AND repaired drafts. This is the alarm case: see both findings rounds.

findings.claim: the GPT-5.6 series ... went to limited preview on June 26, 2026, with GPT-4.5 already retired from ChatGPT that same day
findings.issue: Factually wrong on two counts. (1) OpenAI did not retire any model from ChatGPT on June 26, 2026 alongside the GPT-5.6 preview; the relevant ChatGPT retirements (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, o4-mini, GPT-5 Instant/Thinking) occurred on February 13, 2026, and GPT-5.1 was retired March 11, 2026. (2) There was no 'GPT-4.5' in ChatGPT being retired on that date — this appears to be a fabricated/confused model-and-date pairing. The GPT-5.6 preview date (June 26, 2026) itself is correct, but the retirement clause should be removed or corrected. Note that ChatGPT continued to run GPT-5.5 during the GPT-5.6 limited preview.

findings.claim: OpenAI and Anthropic are now shipping flagship revisions on roughly a monthly cadence
findings.issue: Defensible but loosely stated. It is broadly consistent with the 2026 release pace (e.g., Opus 4.6 Feb, 4.7 April, 4.8 May; Sonnet 5 June 30; GPT-5.6 preview June 26), so it is not blocking, but 'monthly' is a generalization rather than a verified cadence.

findings.claim: In 2026, models from Meta, Mistral, DeepSeek, and Alibaba... Llama 3.1 405B, Mistral Large 2, DeepSeek-V3, and Qwen 2.5 all score competitively on standard benchmarks
findings.issue: This is the core failure mode: the article presents a superseded 2024-era open-model lineup as the current 2026 state. Every one of the four named 'current' models has been replaced by a newer generation. Llama 4 (Scout/Maverick) shipped in April 2025 and is Meta's current generation; Meta even released a closed model, Muse Spark, in April 2026. Mistral's current flagship is Mistral Large 3 (a 41B-active/675B-total MoE under Apache 2.0), part of the Mistral 3 family, not Mistral Large 2. DeepSeek's current flagship is V4 (V4-Pro/V4-Flash), previewed April 24, 2026, not V3. Alibaba's current lineup is Qwen 3.5/3.6 (open) and Qwen 3.7-Max (proprietary, May 2026), not Qwen 2.5. Naming the older generation as what models 'in 2026 routinely' achieve is exactly the stale-as-current framing that must block publication. The article should be updated to the current lineup (Llama 4, Mistral Large 3, DeepSeek V4, Qwen 3.5/3.6).

findings.claim: They don't match the latest GPT-4.5 or Claude 4 on every dimension
findings.issue: GPT-4.5 and Claude 4 are described as 'the latest' closed models, which is badly stale as of the 2026-06-29 article date. OpenAI's current frontier is the GPT-5 generation (GPT-5.5 was the flagship, with GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna previewed June 26, 2026); GPT-4.5 was in fact being retired from ChatGPT around June 26-27, 2026. Anthropic's current frontier is the '5' tier — Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 (June 2026) plus Claude Sonnet 5 (June 30, 2026) and Opus 4.8 (May 2026), not 'Claude 4.' Presenting GPT-4.5/Claude 4 as the current frontier misstates the state of the world by roughly two full model generations.

findings.claim: Their models consistently punch above their weight class... Mistral Large 2 competes directly with much larger models
findings.issue: The Mistral section presents Mistral Large 2 as the current flagship. Mistral's current flagship is Mistral Large 3, released as part of the Mistral 3 family — notably Mistral's first MoE flagship since Mixtral (41B active / 675B total, Apache 2.0). Describing Large 2 as the model that currently 'competes directly with much larger models' presents a superseded model as current.

findings.claim: DeepSeek emerged as a surprise leader, particularly with their R1 reasoning model.
findings.issue: Historically framing R1 (January 2025) as the breakout is fine, but the surrounding section presents R1/V3 as DeepSeek's current contribution. As of the article date, DeepSeek's current flagship is V4 (V4-Pro at 1.6T params/49B active and V4-Flash at 284B/13B, both with 1M-token context), previewed April 24, 2026, with V4-Pro-Max positioned as the best open-source model. The article should reflect V4 as the current DeepSeek generation rather than leaving R1/V3 as the endpoint.

findings.claim: Qwen 2.5 matches the best open models across benchmarks and introduced strong multilingual capabilities.
findings.issue: Qwen 2.5 is stale as the presented-current Alibaba model. Alibaba's current lineup is the Qwen 3.x generation: Qwen 3.5 (February 2026, 397B/17B-active MoE, 201 languages) and Qwen 3.6 open-weight models, plus the proprietary Qwen 3.7-Max (announced May 20, 2026). Presenting Qwen 2.5 as the current benchmark-matching model is a generation-and-a-half out of date.

findings.claim: For many applications... Llama 70B or Mistral Large will do the job at a fraction of the cost.
findings.issue: Consequent to the stale lineup: 'Llama 70B' refers to the Llama 3.x dense 70B tier. Current Llama 4 uses MoE (Scout 17B-active/109B-total, Maverick 17B-active/400B-total), so the practical recommendation should be refreshed to the current models. Not independently blocking beyond the lineup findings, but worth correcting.

findings.claim: Open models also lag on multimodal capabilities. While text-only performance has largely caught up, the best vision-language and audio models remain closed.
findings.issue: This claim is weaker than it was in 2024. Current open releases are natively multimodal (Llama 4 is natively multimodal; Qwen 3.5 unifies text/image/video; DeepSeek V4 added multimodal capabilities). The blanket statement that open multimodal 'lags' and the best VLMs 'remain closed' is now borderline and would benefit from softening, though it is not a hard factual error.
